text: An assert statement is a sanity check — it declares something you believe must be true at that point.
If the condition holds, execution continues silently; if it fails, Python raises an AssertionError.
Here we assert the list isn't empty before averaging, guarding against a divide-by-zero crash.
[chuckle] The optional message after the comma explains what went wrong, making failures easy to diagnose.
[sniff] Asserts are perfect for catching broken assumptions early, close to where the bug actually is.
This one insists a discount percent stays between zero and a hundred, before doing any math.
A valid discount passes right through and computes normally.
[sigh] But an impossible percent trips the assertion, and we catch it with the exact offending value.
[groan] One caution — asserts can be disabled with an optimization flag, so use them for debugging, not for validating real user input.
